title: Hours and closing days
text: Chowk is open Tuesday to Thursday 6:00 pm to 12:30 am, Friday and Saturday 6:00 pm to 1:30 am, and Sunday 6:00 pm to 12:00 am. It is closed all day Monday, because Monday is when the tandoor is rebuilt. The kitchen stops taking orders thirty minutes before closing.

title: Location and parking
text: Chowk is at Plot 42-C, Khayaban-e-Bukhari, Phase VI, DHA, Karachi 75500. There is no signboard; the entrance is a green door set back from the road behind a neem tree. Valet parking runs from 7 pm. Street parking usually fills up by 8 pm on weekends. Ramp access is at the side entrance and the whole restaurant is on the ground floor.

title: Booking a table
text: Bookings open at 6:30 pm; anything earlier is walk-in only. Reserve by phone on +92 21 3584 9002, by WhatsApp on +92 300 214 8871, by email at table@chowk.pk, or through the booking form on the Visit page. Groups larger than eight should call rather than book online. Chowk does not deliver and does not take online food orders.

title: Sikandari Raan
text: Sikandari Raan costs Rs 4,800 and serves four to six people. It is a whole bone-in leg of lamb from Tando Allahyar, marinated for two days in green papaya, mustard oil, ginger, garlic, Kashmiri chilli and dagi mirch, then steamed for four hours in its own stock before ten minutes on the coals for the crust. Medium heat. It is carved at the table and needs two days of notice from the kitchen. It goes well with roghni naan, kachumber and doodh patti.

title: Bihari Boti
text: Bihari Boti costs Rs 1,150 and serves one to two people. Beef undercut is sliced thin against the grain and marinated in papaya, roasted gram flour, fried onion paste, mustard oil and freshly ground garam masala, then charred on skewers. It is the hottest thing on the menu. Order it with roghni naan or dahi baray.

title: Malai Boti
text: Malai Boti costs Rs 1,050 and serves one to two people. Chicken thigh, never breast, in cream, cheddar, hung curd, green chilli, white pepper and lemon. It is mild and it is the dish children usually finish. Pairs with kaali mirch pulao and kachumber.

title: Kata Kat
text: Kata Kat costs Rs 1,400 and serves two to three people. Mutton brain, kidney and heart with a little mince, worked on a flat iron tawa with two heavy blades for about twelve minutes at the open counter. Cooked with tomato, green chilli, ginger julienne, ghee, black pepper and coriander. It is hot. It can be ordered dry or with gravy. Pairs with roghni naan and doodh patti.

title: White Karahi
text: White Karahi costs Rs 1,900 and serves three to four people. Bone-in mutton shoulder cooked in full-fat yoghurt, cream and garlic with coarse black pepper, green chilli and coriander seed. There is no tomato and no colour. Medium heat. Pairs with roghni naan, kachumber and gajar ka halwa.

title: Palak Gosht
text: Palak Gosht costs Rs 1,350 and serves two to three people. Fresh spinach, never frozen and never blended, cooked down for two hours with dill, browned onion and whole cumin, with mutton browned separately and added late. Finished with fried garlic and dried fenugreek. Medium heat. Pairs with roghni naan and dahi baray.

title: Roghni Naan
text: Roghni Naan costs Rs 180 and serves one person. Milk dough rested six hours, topped with sesame and nigella, brushed with ghee and fired in a wood tandoor. No chilli heat. Made to order, so ask for bread first if you are in a hurry.

title: Kaali Mirch Pulao
text: Kaali Mirch Pulao costs Rs 890 and serves two people. Aged sella rice soaked forty minutes and cooked in mutton yakhni with whole black peppercorns, fried onion and ghee, finished on dum. It is not biryani: no layering, no colour, no potato. Mild. Pairs with malai boti and kachumber.

title: Dahi Baray
text: Dahi Baray costs Rs 420 and serves two people. Cold urad dal dumplings soaked in warm water then set in lightly sweetened yoghurt thinned with milk, with tamarind and date chutney, roasted cumin, red chilli and papri. Mild. Pairs with bihari boti and palak gosht.

title: Kachumber
text: Kachumber costs Rs 260 and serves two to three people. Red onion, tomato, cucumber, green chilli and lemon, cut to order rather than in advance, with coriander and black salt served on the side. Mild. Pairs with sikandari raan and white karahi.

title: Gajar ka Halwa
text: Gajar ka Halwa costs Rs 480 and serves two people. Red winter carrots from Sindh reduced in whole milk with sugar for about four hours, finished with khoya, ghee, pistachio and cream, served warm. It is only available from roughly December to February, when the red carrots are in season. Pairs with doodh patti.

title: Doodh Patti
text: Doodh Patti costs Rs 220 per cup. Full cream milk boiled with a Lyari tea blend for eleven minutes and pulled between two vessels before pouring. No water at any stage. Cardamom on request. Ask for less sugar when ordering or it arrives sweet. Pairs with gajar ka halwa and kata kat.

title: Menu overview and mildest dishes
text: The menu has twelve dishes across six sections: Coals (sikandari raan, bihari boti, malai boti), Karahi (kata kat, white karahi, palak gosht), Bread and rice (roghni naan, kaali mirch pulao), Sides (dahi baray, kachumber), Sweet (gajar ka halwa) and Chai (doodh patti). The mildest savoury dishes are malai boti and kaali mirch pulao. The hottest are bihari boti and kata kat. Prices include tax.

title: About Chowk
text: Chowk was opened in 2019 by two cousins in a converted bungalow garage on Khayaban-e-Bukhari, starting with six tables, one cook and four dishes. The wall came down in 2021 so the kata kat could be cooked at an open counter. Sikandari raan was added in 2023 after eleven months of testing. Today there are forty seats, four cooks and twelve dishes. Meat comes from two suppliers in Tando Allahyar, masala is ground fresh at four every morning, and the tandoor is lit with hardwood at four in the afternoon. The room gets loud after nine.

title: Dietary notes and payment
text: There are two vegetarian items, kachumber and dahi baray, plus roghni naan. Everything else contains meat. Guests should tell floor staff about allergies before ordering. Cards and cash are both accepted. There is no delivery and no online food ordering, because charcoal food does not survive the journey.
